title: Cocartesian sections detect a cone of infinity categories being a limit
statement: Use small quasicategories and functor simplicial sets from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], classifying functors from [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], and relative limits and joins from [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $q:X\to C$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories, $K$ a small quasicategory, and $p:K^{\triangleleft}\to C$. Assume the pullback $q_p:E=X\times_C K^{\triangleleft}\to K^{\triangleleft}$ is a cocartesian fibration, classified by $\chi:K^{\triangleleft}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ (in a larger universe). Let $\Gamma$ be the full subcategory of the simplicial set of sections of $q_p$ spanned by sections carrying every edge to a $q_p$-cocartesian edge, and define $\Gamma_K$ similarly over $K$. Morphisms in these full subcategories are arbitrary transformations over the base. Restriction $r:\Gamma\to\Gamma_K$ is an isofibration of quasicategories (an inner fibration lifting each equivalence edge with any specified source). The diagram $\chi$ is a limit diagram if and only if $r$ is an equivalence. If every cocartesian section $s:K^{\triangleleft}\to E$, composed into $X$, is a $q$-limit diagram, then $r$ is fully faithful. Under this last hypothesis, $\chi$ is a limit diagram if and only if every vertex of $\Gamma_K$ extends to an actual vertex of $\Gamma$ (with exactly the specified restriction). Empty $K$ is allowed.

source.place: Higher Algebra Remark B.0.26, printed p.1469, including the mapping-space argument and the categorical-fibration/surjective-on-vertices assertion; its cited Higher Topos Theory Proposition 3.3.3.1. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Put $L=K^{\triangleleft}$ and for $T=L,K$ (using the inclusion $K\hookrightarrow L$), let $\mathcal S_T=\operatorname{Fun}_{/L}(T,E)$ denote all sections over $T$, i.e. the strict fiber of $\operatorname{Fun}(T,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(T,L)$ over the inclusion $T\hookrightarrow L$. The cocartesian fibration $q_p$ is a Joyal fibration by [lem-coef-cocartesian-joyal-fibration], hence an isofibration by [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](1). Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$ and to $K\hookrightarrow L$ with $q_p:E\to L$: both corner maps are isofibrations between quasicategories. The first is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)$; its strict fiber $\mathcal S_K$ over a vertex is a quasicategory, since an inner horn in the fiber lies over a degenerate simplex. Pull the second corner map back along $\mathcal S_K\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)}\operatorname{Fun}(L,L)$, $a\mapsto(a,1_L)$. The resulting map is exactly $R:\mathcal S_L\to\mathcal S_K$, and $\mathcal S_L$ is a quasicategory as a pullback of an inner fibration over the quasicategory $\mathcal S_K$. By [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](1) the corner map is a Joyal fibration, i.e. has the right lifting property against all injective categorical equivalences; this property is stable under pullback, so $R$ is a Joyal fibration between quasicategories. Applying (1) again, now to $R$ itself, $R$ is an inner fibration that lifts every equivalence edge of $\mathcal S_K$ with any prescribed source to an edge that is an equivalence in $\mathcal S_L$ (not merely in $\operatorname{Fun}(L,E)$). Thus $R$ is an isofibration of quasicategories.

source.place: B.0.26, categorical-fibration assertion; HTT Proposition 3.3.1.7 and Kerodon Proposition 4.4.5.1 supply the all-section corner map

proof.text: The cocartesian sections form a replete full subcategory of each $\mathcal S_T$. Indeed an equivalence $a\simeq b$ in $\mathcal S_T$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(T,E)$ (the inclusion carries the inverse and its two witnessing $2$-simplices along), hence pointwise an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. For an edge $e:t\to t'$, its naturality square identifies $a(e)$ and $b(e)$ up to equivalences of their endpoints over identity base edges. In the mapping-space square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], pre- and postcomposition by these endpoint equivalences induce equivalences on the two upper spaces (their inverses are composition with the inverse edges, using [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]); the lower spaces are unchanged. Homotopy-pullback invariance [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] therefore says that $a(e)$ is cocartesian exactly when $b(e)$ is. The full subcategories $\Gamma,\Gamma_K$ are quasicategories by the functor-category calculus. An inner-horn lift for $R$ with all given vertices in $\Gamma$ has all its vertices in $\Gamma$ and so lies in this full subcategory. An equivalence lift for $R$ starting in $\Gamma$ ends there by repleteness. Hence $r:\Gamma\to\Gamma_K$ is an isofibration, with the specified source-lifting property.

source.place: B.0.26, justification of the categorical-fibration assertion on the full cocartesian-section subcategories

proof.text:
For $T=L$ or $K$, write $E_T=E\times_L T$, $\chi_T=\chi|_T$, and $\Gamma_T$ for its cocartesian sections. The straightening theorem identifies this pullback with $\chi_T$. For every small quasicategory $A$, section currying and straightening give natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}_\infty}(A,\Gamma_T)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(A,\Gamma_T)^\simeq\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{coCart}(T)}(T\times A,E_T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(T,\operatorname{Cat}_\infty)}(\Delta_T A,\chi_T).$$
Here [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] supplies the mapping-space model for $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$; [lem-cbc-cocartesian-section-currying] supplies currying with arbitrary transformations and identifies $T\times A$ with the constant classifying diagram; [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] supplies the last equivalence. The evaluation $T\times\Gamma_T\to E_T$ therefore gives a cone $\lambda_T:\Delta_T\Gamma_T\to\chi_T$. The displayed equivalence is exactly postcomposition with this cone, by the evaluation clause of currying. The cone mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that $\lambda_T$ is limiting. The cited restriction compatibilities identify the map of these cones for $K\hookrightarrow L$ with the actual restriction $r$. This uses neither a strict diagram nor an ordinary indexing category.

source.place: HTT proof of Proposition 3.3.3.1, the derived diagonal/section adjunction, and Corollary 3.3.3.2; direct assembly of existing mapping-space comparisons

proof.text: Let $v$ be the new vertex of $L=\Delta^0\star K$. The join construction gives a coherent transformation $\eta:\Delta_L v\to1_L$: on a simplex of $L$ it uses the same simplex with an initial vertex $v$ inserted; at $v$ its component is the identity. Thus $\chi\eta$ is a cone on $\chi$ with apex $\chi(v)$. For every $A$, evaluation at $v$ sends a transformation $\beta:\Delta_L A\to\chi$ to $\beta_v:A\to\chi(v)$. Its inverse sends $a$ to $(\chi\eta)\circ\Delta_La$. One composite is the identity because $\eta_v=1_v$; the other is coherently equivalent to the identity by the naturality of $\beta$ on $\eta$. This calculation is on coherent transformations with all parameter simplices, so gives inverse maps of their mapping spaces. The cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $\chi\eta$ limiting. Together with step 3, uniqueness of limiting cones from the same calculus shows that evaluation $e_v:\Gamma\to E_v\simeq\chi(v)$ is an equivalence. Its compatibility with the cones follows from the evaluation and transport compatibilities in section currying and straightening.

source.place: HTT Corollary 3.3.3.2, proof, evaluation at the initial vertex (opposite convention); explicit contraction of the left join cone

proof.text: The boundary of $\lambda_L$ is the cone obtained by composing $r$ with $\lambda_K$, by step 3. Under $e_v$ of step 4, this is precisely the cone $\chi(v)\to\chi|_K$ supplied by $\chi$. Since $\lambda_K$ is limiting, this cone is limiting if and only if its comparison $\Gamma\xrightarrow{r}\Gamma_K$ is an equivalence: the cone mapping-space criterion identifies its tests with $\operatorname{Map}(A,r)$, and the fully faithful Yoneda functor of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] detects equivalences. Explicitly, if all these maps are equivalences, testing $A=\Gamma_K$ gives a right inverse to $r$, and testing $A=\Gamma$ then gives the other inverse identity; [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] identifies these identities with equivalence in $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. The converse follows by composing with a quasi-inverse. This proves the first equivalence without the relative-limit hypothesis.

source.place: B.0.26, first equivalence, expanded using the section/diagonal comparison of HTT 3.3.3.1

proof.text:
Now assume every cocartesian section, viewed in $X$, is a $q$-limit diagram. Fix $s',s\in\Gamma$. For $T=L,K$, the map $\operatorname{Fun}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Fun}(T,C)$ is an inner fibration: an inner-horn lifting problem is adjoint to the pushout-product of that horn with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow T$, which is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. Consequently its induced maps on mapping spaces are Kan fibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber]. Apply the defining relative-limit square [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] for $s$ to the source test diagram $s'$. Denote its four corners by $A,B,C_0,D$ in upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right order; it gives $A\simeq B\times_D^h C_0$. Take its homotopy fiber over $1_p\in C_0$. Homotopy-pullback pasting gives
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{1_p}(A\to C_0)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{1_{p|_K}}(B\to D).$$
By [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] these are the strict fibers of the Kan fibrations above. Degreewise, a right-pinched mapping simplex belongs to that strict fiber exactly when its projected diagram is constant at $p$ (respectively $p|_K$). Thus they are $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_L}(s',s)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_K}(s'|_K,s|_K)$, and the equivalence is restriction. Fullness of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma_K$ leaves these mapping spaces unchanged. Hence $r$ is fully faithful.

source.place: B.0.26, mapping-space argument; relative universality in the precise form of Kerodon 7.1.6.19(2)

proof.text: Under the same hypothesis, full faithfulness is now established. By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], $r$ is an equivalence exactly when it is essentially surjective: if its full essential image is all of $\Gamma_K$, the cited quasi-inverse is a quasi-inverse to $r$; the other direction follows from a quasi-inverse. Essential surjectivity means that for each $t\in\Gamma_K$ there are $s\in\Gamma$ and an equivalence $r(s)\to t$. The isofibration proved in steps 1-2 lifts this very edge with source $s$, to an equivalence $s\to\widetilde s$ with $r(\widetilde s)=t$ exactly. Conversely an exact extension witnesses essential surjectivity using the identity. Combining this with step 5 proves the final equivalence. If $K=\varnothing$, then $L=\Delta^0$, $\Gamma=E_v$, and $\Gamma_K=\Delta^0$. For $t,s\in E_v$, the relative-limit square identifies the mapping space in the fiber, namely the strict fiber of $\operatorname{Map}_X(t,s)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(p(v),p(v))$ over $1_{p(v)}$, with a point. Thus every object of $E_v$ is terminal in the fiber, and full faithfulness follows, and exact extension is precisely nonemptiness of $E_v$, which makes it equivalent to the terminal category. If $E_v$ is empty, the relative-limit hypothesis is vacuous and both the limit assertion and exact extension fail. Thus the empty case is included.

source.place: B.0.26, essential-surjectivity versus surjectivity-on-vertices argument, including the empty indexing shape
